subject: Human Evolution
title: Gender Roles Revisited
description: A fast breakdown of Gender Roles Revisited for builders.

hook.text: A 9,000-year-old burial in Peru held a woman with a full hunting toolkit. She wasn't an exception.

buildup.text: Analysis of burials across the Americas found that 30–50% of big-game hunters may have been female.

discovery.text: The 'man the hunter' narrative assumed rigid sex roles—but the evidence increasingly says otherwise.

twist.text: Ice age survival likely demanded flexibility: everyone who could contribute to a hunt probably did.

climax.text: Rigid gender roles may be a product of farming societies, not an ice age universal.

punchline.text: Survival didn't care who held the spear.

quiz.question: What does recent evidence say about ice age gender roles?
options: Women participated in big-game hunting more than previously thought
